On Tuesday, August 25, 2026, I completed batch `4` step-5 authoring for the full `localisation-of-modules-and-support` A/B pair: 35 A-page items, 10 B-page examples, and both page files. The step-5 audit report is appended to [research/frontier-19-batch-4.notes.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-19-batch-4.notes.md), and the authored pages are [localisation-of-modules-and-support.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/library/commutative-algebra/localisation-of-modules-and-support.md) and [localisation-of-modules-and-support-examples.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/library/commutative-algebra/localisation-of-modules-and-support-examples.md).

- Scoped `precheck`: all 42 proof-bearing items pass; the 3 definitions are `verification.precheck: n/a`.
- `proof-contract --strict`: 0 errors, 1 warning (`shotgun-bracket` on `thm-local-criterion-for-zero-modules-and-maps`).
- `coverage-checklist`, `content-policy`, and `validate-plan`: pass.
- `prosecheck`: 0 errors, 4 warnings; all 4 warnings are the existing count-in-prose lines in the batch notes, not in the authored page prose.
- Global `depcheck` and `fwdcheck` still fail on unrelated existing repository issues outside batch `4`. Filtering those outputs produced no batch-4-local hits. `extcheck` and `citecheck` likewise produced no batch-4-local matches.

Notable authoring outcome:
- I removed the step-4 intra-order defect on `thm-support-of-a-tensor-product-of-finite-modules` by replacing the forward same-page Nakayama dependency with an earlier inline local argument based on the adjugate identity.
- No scaffolded item id or title was dropped or narrowed. The exact `deps` deltas from scaffold to authored text are recorded in the step-5 ledger in the notes file.

Confidence is moderate to high on the batch-local mathematics and mechanics. I did not run `rendercheck.mjs`, `finite-smoke.mjs`, `risk-report.mjs`, `boundary-audit.mjs`, or `citation-fidelity.mjs`, and I did not re-run `source-fetch-check --stamp` after authoring because the sandbox DNS blocker recorded in the notes still applies here.
